subject: Civil Engineering
title: Gravity Dams
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Gravity Dams.

hook.text: A gravity dam is pure mass — it holds back water simply by being heavy enough to resist.

buildup.text: Concrete or masonry stacked in a triangular profile — wide base, narrow crest.

discovery.text: The dam's weight pushes down on the foundation — friction prevents it from sliding.

twist.text: Uplift pressure — water seeping under the dam — reduces effective weight and threatens stability.

climax.text: Drainage galleries inside the dam relieve uplift — collecting seepage before it undermines.

punchline.text: A gravity dam wins by weight. The heavier it is, the harder the water pushes in vain.

quiz.question: What is the main threat to a gravity dam's stability?
options: Wind blowing against the upstream face
Uplift pressure from water seeping under the dam, reducing its effective weight
Thermal expansion cracking the concrete during summer

details.summary: Gravity dams resist the horizontal force of water purely through their own weight. They are massive structures, typically made of concrete or masonry, with a triangular cross-section that is widest at the base. Their stability comes from gravity keeping them firmly pressed against the foundation.
details.whyItMatters: Gravity dams are among the most common and reliable dam types because their stability mechanism is simple and well-understood. They suit a wide range of site conditions and height requirements.
takeaways: Stability relies entirely on the weight of the dam resisting water pressure
A triangular cross-section provides weight efficiently where needed most
The Grand Coulee Dam in the United States is a famous gravity dam

faq.question: Why does a gravity dam need to be so massive?
faq.answer: Water pressure increases linearly with depth, reaching enormous forces at a tall dam's base. The dam's weight must exceed the overturning moment from water pressure with an adequate safety factor. The triangular profile concentrates mass at the base where overturning forces are greatest.

faq.question: What are the main failure modes for a gravity dam?
faq.answer: Overturning occurs when water pressure exceeds the dam's resisting moment. Sliding happens when horizontal water force exceeds friction at the foundation contact. Overstressing occurs when internal compressive or tensile stresses exceed material capacity.
